channel.title: TidyDesk Studio Guides
channel.description: Spreadsheet guides for small businesses and households

item.title: Year-End Records for the Self-Employed: What to Gather Before You Sit Down With Your Accountant
item.description: A practical checklist of the income, expense and mileage records a sole trader or freelancer should gather at year end.

item.title: How to Budget Paycheck by Paycheck When Your Bills Don't Line Up With the Calendar Month
item.description: How to split a budget by pay date instead of by month, assigning each bill to the paycheck that will cover it.

item.title: How to Track Bridal Makeup Bookings, Trials and Deposits So No Date Gets Double-Booked
item.description: A simple way for freelance makeup artists to keep bookings, trial sessions, deposits and balances in one sheet.

item.title: How to Track Sponsored Posts and Brand Deals So Nothing Slips Through
item.description: A spreadsheet layout for content creators to follow each sponsorship from first email to deliverables, due dates and payment.

item.title: How to Schedule Rental Turnover Cleans and Pay Your Cleaners Correctly
item.description: How to plan same-day turnover cleans between guests and keep a clear record of who cleaned what and what each cleaner is owed.

item.title: How to Track Grocery Costs and Menus for Each Personal Chef Client
item.description: How personal chefs and meal prep cooks can log menus, receipts and client notes so every client's grocery cost and margin is clear.

item.title: How to Work Out Your Freelance Hourly Rate and Price a Project Without Guessing
item.description: A step-by-step way to turn your income goal, expenses and unpaid hours into an hourly rate, then into a fixed project price.

item.title: How to Compare Houses You Have Viewed So You Can Actually Decide
item.description: A simple scoring method for comparing homes after viewings, with weighted criteria, a worked example and the mistakes that muddy a decision.

item.title: How to Keep Track of Recurring Cleaning Clients, Jobs and Payments
item.description: A simple spreadsheet layout for a small cleaning business to schedule recurring jobs, record what each client is owed and see who hasn't paid.

item.title: How to Track Photography Bookings, Deposits and Shoot Deliveries in One Sheet
item.description: A simple spreadsheet layout for photographers to follow every client from enquiry to deposit, shoot day and final gallery delivery.

item.title: How to Keep Track of Pet Sitting Visits, Holiday Bookings and Who Has Paid
item.description: A practical spreadsheet setup for pet sitters and dog walkers to log visits, handle holiday rates and see unpaid balances at a glance.

item.title: How to Track Personal Training Sessions and Prepaid Packages Without Losing Count
item.description: How independent trainers can log sessions, count down prepaid packages and spot expiring or unpaid clients with a simple spreadsheet.

item.title: How to Track Vacation Rental Bookings and Expenses to See Your Real Profit
item.description: How a short-term rental host can log bookings, expenses and per-stay profit in a spreadsheet, with formulas for occupancy and average nightly rate.

item.title: How to Track Tutoring Lessons and Payments So Every Session Is Paid For
item.description: A spreadsheet method for private tutors to log lessons, packages and payments and see at a glance who owes what.

item.title: How to Track Grant Deadlines and Reporting Dates So Nothing Slips
item.description: A simple spreadsheet layout for tracking grant applications, award conditions and report due dates at a small nonprofit.

item.title: How to Track Volunteer Hours and Shifts Without Chasing Anyone
item.description: How a small group can log volunteer shifts, total hours per person and spot gaps in cover, using a simple spreadsheet layout.

item.title: How to Work Out the Cost of One Portion When You Cook for Sale
item.description: A step-by-step method for turning ingredient prices into a true cost per portion, including yield loss, and a selling price you can defend.

item.title: How to Keep Track of Freelance Leads So Nobody Goes Quiet on You
item.description: A simple pipeline layout for freelancers: stages, follow-up dates and a few formulas that show which leads need a message today.

item.title: How to Build a Wedding Budget That Survives Contact With Real Quotes
item.description: A step-by-step way to split a wedding budget into categories, track estimates versus actual quotes, and keep the guest count honest.

item.title: How to Track Job Applications and Never Miss a Follow-Up
item.description: Set up a simple spreadsheet to log applications, interview stages and follow-up dates so nothing falls through the cracks during a job search.

item.title: How to Keep a Car Maintenance Log and Work Out Your Real Fuel Economy
item.description: A simple spreadsheet setup for logging oil changes, repairs and fill-ups, plus the formula that shows your true miles per gallon.

item.title: How to Plan a Home Move: A Week-by-Week Checklist and Budget
item.description: A practical timeline and budget layout for moving house, with the costs people most often forget.

item.title: How to Keep Track of Household Bills So Nothing Gets Paid Late
item.description: A simple way to list every recurring bill, see what is due next and stop paying late fees by accident.

item.title: How to Compare Contractor Bids and Keep a Renovation on Budget
item.description: How to line up contractor quotes fairly and track real spending against your renovation budget.

item.title: How to Track Your Net Worth Month by Month (A Simple 10-Minute Routine)
item.description: A plain routine for listing every account and debt, logging balances once a month and seeing whether your overall position is actually improving.

item.title: How to Set Reorder Points So You Stop Running Out of Your Best Sellers
item.description: A practical way for small shops and makers to log stock movements, work out days of stock left and set a reorder point for each item before the holiday rush.

item.title: How to Tell If a Craft Fair Was Actually Worth It (After the Booth Fee and Everything Else)
item.description: A simple way to work out real profit, profit per hour and sell-through for each craft fair or market, so you know which events to book again.

item.title: Why Is My Utility Bill Higher? How to Tell If You Used More or Just Paid More
item.description: A step-by-step way to compare power, gas and water bills against the same month last year and split a higher bill into extra usage versus a higher price.

item.title: How to Track Donations and Thank-You Notes for a Small Nonprofit (Before the Year-End Rush)
item.description: A simple way for small nonprofits, clubs and community groups to log every gift, send thank-yous on time and spot supporters who haven't given yet this year.

item.title: How to Track Payments to Contractors and Freelancers So Year-End Totals Take Minutes
item.description: A simple payments log for small businesses that pay freelancers, subcontractors and vendors, with per-payee yearly totals and a paperwork check.
